vars.CHARACTER: A kind grandpa moose train conductor: dark-brown fur, a big rounded tan muzzle with two large dark nostrils, small black eyes, bushy cream eyebrows, round ears and broad flat antlers. Navy conductor cap with a gold band and a round gold badge, red scarf with a small gold bell, navy vest with three gold buttons and a gold belt buckle over a cream long-sleeved shirt, brown trousers, dark-brown hoof hands and hooves.

IMAGE ROLES:
image_1 = CHARACTER DESIGN. Take from it only who the character is: species, body proportions, costume, colours and accessories. If it shows several views, use them all to understand the design.
image_2 and image_3 = ART STYLE. Animation atlases of two characters already shipped in this game, a hippo and a raccoon, cut into separate parts. Take from them only how things are painted: shading, colour, edges, level of detail and the chunky shape language. Their species, costumes and layout are not part of this picture.

TASK:
Paint the character from image_1 as one finished full-body character in the art style of image_2 and image_3, as a clean master drawing for cutting into animation parts.

ART STYLE (taken from the shipped characters in the style images):
Soft digital painting for a bright casual mobile game, matching the shipped hippo and raccoon exactly. Every shape is a big, chunky, simplified mass with a soft rounded silhouette, slightly swollen and squashy, like a soft toy. Heads and hands are generous in size; hands are fat mittens with three or four short rounded fingers. Interior detail is minimal: a shape reads from its silhouette and its colour.
Shading is smooth airbrushed volume. Each shape has one broad lit side, one broad soft shaded side and a gentle lighter bounce along the shaded edge, blended with smooth gradients. A few soft darker shapes suggest a fold, a pocket or a crease, painted as soft blurred patches. Highlights are broad and soft.
Colour is bright, clean and saturated: candy violet, turquoise, orange, golden yellow, warm mauve. Shadows shift hue toward violet or blue on cool colours and toward red on warm colours, and stay clean and colourful.
Edges are clean and slightly soft. Shapes are separated from each other only by colour and value. There is no outline, contour line or ink line anywhere, and no dark stroke around any shape.
Surfaces are smooth. Fur is shown by a few soft tufts along the silhouette and a gently mottled gradient, never by drawn strands. Cloth, wood and metal are smooth painted colour with a soft highlight, with no grain, weave or texture.
Eyes are simple glossy dark ovals with one small white highlight, set into soft eye areas; noses and nostrils are simple soft dark shapes.

POSE AND FRAMING:
Front view, facing the viewer, in a symmetrical rest pose. Both arms hang down and out at about thirty degrees from the sides, so plain background shows between each arm and the body along the whole arm. Hands open and relaxed. Legs straight, feet a little apart and flat on the ground. Head level, looking at the viewer, with a gentle closed-mouth smile and eyes open. The whole character fits in the frame with an even margin around it and fills about eighty-five percent of its height. The background is one flat plain light grey with nothing else in it, and the character stands on it without any cast shadow.

FINAL CHECK:
1. Painted like the shipped hippo and raccoon: airbrushed soft volume, candy colours, chunky simplified shapes, smooth surfaces, no outlines.
2. Clearly the same character as image_1: same costume pieces and colours.
3. Front view, symmetrical, arms clear of the body, full body in frame.
4. Flat light grey background, single character, no text.

TASK:
Repaint the character from image_1 as a sheet of separate body pieces for 2D skeletal animation in Spine. Each piece is painted whole, including the area that is normally hidden under the piece in front of it, so that the pieces can rotate at their joints without showing gaps. Joint ends are rounded.

THE PIECES (each painted exactly once, paired pieces painted twice, once for each side):
Head base: the head with its fixed features such as the snout, muzzle, nose or beak and its nostrils. The forehead, the eye areas and the mouth area are plain smooth skin, fur or feathers in the head's own colour, because the eyebrows, eyes and mouth are separate pieces on another sheet. Its lower edge is complete all the way round.
Head items, each as its own piece: every hat or cap, every horn or antler, each ear, and any hair tuft on top of the head. The eyes, eyebrows and mouth belong only to the face sheet, so this sheet has no eyes, no eyebrows, no eye patches and no mouths.
Neck items, each as its own piece: every scarf, collar, tie or necklace, and any small item hanging from it such as a bell, medal or pendant.
Torso: the chest and belly with whatever top the character wears, continuing up into a short neck, painted complete where the neck items and the head would cover it.
Each arm is cut into THREE separate pieces with empty background between them: the upper arm from shoulder to elbow, the forearm from elbow to wrist, and the hand, open and relaxed, with a short wrist stub.
Hips: the waist and the top of whatever covers the hips, with rounded leg openings.
Each leg is cut into TWO separate pieces with empty background between them: the leg from hip to ankle, and the foot, hoof, paw or shoe.
A tail, if the character has one, and every prop the character carries, each as its own piece.

LAYOUT IN ROWS, read left to right:
Row 1: head base, then the head items.
Row 2: the neck items, the torso, the two upper arms.
Row 3: the two forearms, the two hands, the hips.
Row 4: the two legs, the two feet, then any tail and props.
All pieces are laid out on one flat plain light grey background. Every piece stands apart from every other piece with a clear gap of empty background around it, at least as wide as one of the character's fingers. Pieces never touch, never overlap, and stay fully inside the frame. Each piece is shown flat, facing the viewer, upright, and all pieces share one scale. The sheet contains only these pieces, with no labels, numbers, text, guides or shadows.

FINAL CHECK:
1. Every piece is clearly cut from the character in image_1, in its colours and painting.
2. Each arm is in three pieces and each leg in two; every head item and neck item is separate from the head and torso; no eyes, eyebrows or mouths anywhere on the sheet.
3. Painted like the shipped atlas: airbrushed soft volume, smooth surfaces, no outlines; joint ends rounded and hidden areas painted complete.
4. Every piece separated by empty background; flat light grey background; no text.

TASK:
Paint the facial features of the character from image_1 as a sheet of separate swappable pieces for facial animation in Spine, so each piece drops straight onto the head base.

THE PIECES (each painted exactly once):
Scale anchor: the character's head base, meaning the head from image_1 with its snout, muzzle, nose or beak and nostrils, and with plain eye areas and a plain mouth area. Leave out every hat, horn, antler, ear and hair tuft. Every other piece on this sheet is painted at exactly the size it has on this head.
Left eye open and right eye open, each on a small soft patch of the head's own skin, fur or feathers.
Left eye closed and right eye closed, a gentle downward-curved closed eyelid on the same small patch.
Left eyebrow and right eyebrow in their relaxed position, if the character has eyebrows.
Left eyebrow raised and right eyebrow raised, arched up in surprise, if the character has eyebrows.
Mouth smile: the character's gentle closed smile, on a small patch of the surface around the mouth.
Mouth open happy: a wide open smiling mouth with a dark-red inside and a pink tongue, on the same kind of patch.
Mouth O: a small round open mouth, as when saying "oh", on the same kind of patch.
Mouth sad: a gentle downturned closed mouth, on the same kind of patch.

LAYOUT IN ROWS, read left to right:
Row 1: the scale anchor head base.
Row 2: the four eyes.
Row 3: the four eyebrows.
Row 4: the four mouths.
All pieces are laid out on one flat plain light grey background. Every piece stands apart from every other piece with a clear gap of empty background around it, at least as wide as one of the character's fingers. Pieces never touch, never overlap, and stay fully inside the frame. Each piece is shown flat, facing the viewer, upright, and all pieces share one scale. The sheet contains only these thirteen pieces, painted fully opaque, with no faint, ghosted or half-transparent shapes anywhere, and with no labels, numbers, text, guides or shadows.

FINAL CHECK:
1. The head base is the head from image_1 without its hat, horns or ears, and every feature is sized to fit on it.
2. Every piece matches the colours and painting of the face in image_1.
3. Painted like the shipped atlas: airbrushed soft volume, smooth, no outlines.
4. Every piece separated by empty background; flat light grey background; no text.
